University of Nebraska Omaha (UNO)

Established in 1869, the University of Nebraska Omaha is a public research university located in the heart of Omaha, the largest city of the U.S. state of Nebraska, situated on the west bank of the Missouri River. Then, in 1908, the Omaha Presbyterian Theological Seminary faculty was founded.

As a private non-sectarian college, the university was originally known as the University of Omaha, a place meant to provide Christian-based education free from ecclesiastical control. Indeed, UNO used to serve as a bold alternative to the city’s many successful religiously affiliated institutions.

Ranked as 151 top national universities through the Lincoln’s ranking, the university has increased its students' numbers by opening new dormitories and academic space. It has also recently constructed modern facilities for its engineering, information technology, business, and biomechanics programs.

UNO currently offers more than 200 programs of study across 6 different colleges, with student, athletic, and research facilities spread between 3 campuses.

Today, more than 24,000 students study at UNO, including more than 1,600 international students. UNO is committed to welcoming international students as part of its global mission.
administrative:
1. Application Dossier

You will work directly with the partner university regarding your application. All required documents will have to be uploaded on their platform or sent by email before the deadline. (See the Americas Teams channel for each application deadline.) If you have not received anything yet, it means your nomination has not been sent yet — please be patient.


In the past, the partner has asked for the following:

  • Application form after the link is sent, must be completed
  • Proof of English proficiency
  • Proof of financial eligibility with the UNO Financial Affidavit for inbound exchange students.
  • Students must show proof of funds for education and living expenses for the duration of their studies at UNO.
  • Submit a bank statement, financial statement, or letter from your bank with a minimum balance of $20,000.
  • Financial documents must be less than 6 months old.
  • Copy of passport
  • Health Insurance is mandatory and must be purchased through the UNO student health insurance plan.

This information is subject to change by the partner university. They will provide you with the most current information upon your acceptance.


To be given to Epitech bachelor campus administration to reenroll for the Tech4 (in April/May):

  • The addendum to the contract
  • EPITECH re-registration dossier

This information is subject to change by the partner university. They will provide you with the most current information upon your acceptance.


2. Visa (more information here)

You can find all the detailed information on the US government website or the Embassy of the US in Paris website. You can check the deadlines for obtaining an appointment here.


1/ Admission letter and I-20 form

Once you are admitted by the host university, UNO will send us your admission package with your acceptance letter and original documents for your visa. You can request a visa only after your application has been approved. After the visa application, proceed to the course enrollment and housing applications on your MavLINK student account.

Please check the information on I-20 carefully and sign the document.


2/ Pay the SEVIS fees

 You must then pay the SEVIS I-901 fees online (here). Make sure you print the receipts. The fees for students are $350.


3/Complete the DS-160 form

Complete DS-160 form and upload an ID photo meeting the following requirements. Print the application form confirmation page to bring to your interview.

You will have to pay a visa application fee (non refundable) before your interview of $185 (more information here).


4/Schedule an appointment at the consulate

For people in France, you need to make an appointment for your interview at the US Consulate. Plan to travel to Paris for it.

If you live in another country, check the different consulate/embassy.


During your interview at the consulate, you must:

  • have the necessary supporting documents to prove that you qualify for the category of visa that you request--document relating to your current studies and its relationship to the studies you wish to pursue in the United States: academic transcript, various certificates, SAT or TOEFL test scores, diplomas, etc.
  • demonstrate, with supporting evidence, to the consular officer that you have solid family, social and financial ties to France and that you intend to return there once your residence permit has expired.
  • prove that you have the financial means necessary to finance your studies and live in good conditions in the United States for the first 12 months. Any document proving your family or relational ties with any person funding your studies, as well as bank statements, tax notices thereof.

Please note that the visa gives you the right to work 20 hours on campus.


3.Insurance and Health (more information here)

International J-1 scholars and their dependents must have health insurance from a U.S.-based medical insurance company that pays for health care in Nebraska to maintain nonimmigrant status. UNO has a few specific health insurance options for scholars to meet these federal requirements.


Health insurance coverage for J-1 and J-2 visa holders must include:

  1. Medical benefits of at least $100,000 per illness or accident.
  2. Deductible not to exceed $500 per accident or illness.
  3. Medical evacuation benefit in the amount of $50,000.
  4. Payment for repatriation of remains in the event of death in the amount of $25,000.


The insurance corporation underwriting the insurance policy must meet or exceed the following ratings:

  • A.M. Best or Insurance Solvency International rating of A-
  • Standard & Poor’s claims-paying ability rating of A-
  • Weiss Research, Inc. rating of B+


In addition, UNO requires international students to submit an official copy of the required immunizations and complete a tuberculosis test.

For more information, you can consult the country’s health file at: https://www.pasteur.fr/fr/centre-medical/preparer-son-voyage/etats-unis

Note: It is advisable to register on the French register established outside France and to report to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs via the Ariane platform: https://pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fildariane/dyn/public/login.html.


4. Prepare your arrival

When arriving to Omaha, transportation from the airport is available upon request at: go.unomaha.edu/gettingstarted

International students must attend the orientation day.

For advice to travelers issued by the Ministry of Europe and Foreign Affairs on the host country, click here.
accomodation:
On-campus accommodation (more information here)

You can apply through the MavLINK portal. You need to choose between:

  • University Village
  • Maverick Village (on the main Dodge Street campus)
  • Scott Village (on the Scott campus)

All dormitories are close to dining, shopping, parks, and other entertainment options. UNO offers free shuttle buses between Dodge and Scott campus.

$260 for deposit/application fee when signing a housing contract.

Prices go between 7000 and 8000$ for annual lease contracts.


Off-campus accommodation (more information here)

UNO mentions two options:

  1. St. John Paul II Newman Center
  2. Lozier Hall at College St. Mary

Housing rates: from $7,000 to $9,000 per academic year.

cost:
Financial Overview (4th year Epitech)

  • You must pay the tuition fees for the 4th year of EPITECH, as well as the re-registration fees and related fees.
  • EPITECH covers the tuition fees. Epitech covers tuition only for required credits.
  • The tuition supplement payable by you is indicated at the top of this page (if applicable).
  • Other costs at your expense include: travel, accommodation on site, insurance, and everyday expenses (books, food, transport, etc.)


Other Expenses / estimated budget (more information here)

The local currency is the Dollar. 1 € = 1.16USD (rate as of October 2025).

Please check the Numbeo website to compare the cost of living between your city of origin and your city of exchange. Please note that everyone's budget will be different according to one's lifestyle.


Living in Omaha, Nebraska, is cheaper than living in New York or San Francisco. There is no need for a car since everything is on campus and public transport is available.

  • Round trip flights: about 1000€, depending on the airline & travel dates
  • Health insurance: $4000/year
  • Visa application fees: about 500€
  • Standard fee: $184/year
  • Books and supplies: 1000$
  • Deposit/application fee if you live on campus: 260$
  • Transportation: 1600$/ year (if you live off campus)
  • Housing & food: 13500$/ year
  • Personal expenses (leisure...): 2500$/year


These prices are indicative and may vary.
